==============
Fisher is now based on the count of interval overlaps, subject to `-f`.
We can compare the output of fisher on simulated data by running `python sim.py`
which will show the output from `bedtools fisher` and then running `bash shuf.sh`
which will repeatedly run
```Shell
bedtools intersect -wo -a taa.bed -b <(bedtools shuffle -allowBeyondChromEnd   -i tbb.bed -g tgg.genome) | wc -l
```
and then report the proportion of times that number is >= the observed intersection.
In `sim.py` changing the lenght of the intervals (via `maxA`, `maxB`) has the greatest effect on the
correspondence of the simulated p-value from `shuf.sh` and the one from `fisher`. The right-tailed p-value
from `fisher` should correspond well to the value from the simulation.

events.text:
Fixed and verified. `python reproduce.py` now exits 0 with `public_reproduction_passed: true`.

**Root cause** — `source/src/fisher/fisher.cpp:34`. The chromsweep stops as soon as the query hits EOF, so any database records positioned after the last query interval are never consumed. `NewChromSweep::closeOut(bool)` is the documented drain step ("You MUST call this method after sweep if you want the getTotalRecordLength methods to return the whole length of the record files", `source/src/utils/NewChromsweep/NewChromsweep.h:45`), but its database-draining loop only runs when called with `true` (`NewChromsweep.cpp:81-91`). Fisher called the no-argument `closeOut()`, which drains the query tail but not the database tail, so `getDatabaseTotalRecords()` returned only the records the sweep happened to scan. Valid appended background intervals (e.g. chromosomes absent from the query) were silently dropped from "Number of db intervals" and from the Fisher table/p-values — the augmented fixture reported db=3 instead of 6, with p-values identical to the core run.

**Fix** — one line: `Fisher::finalizeCalculations()` now calls `_sweep->closeOut(true)`, exactly as the sibling `Jaccard::finalizeCalculations()` (`source/src/jaccard/jaccard.cpp:37`) already does. Since fisher requires a genome file, `testChromOrder` short-circuits internally, so the `true` flag only enables the database-drain loop; no behavior changes for chrom-order checking. Nothing is hard-coded — the fix is at the sweep/context level and applies to any BED input.

**Verification**
- Public reproduction: was EXIT=1 (`reported_database_delta=0`, `pvalue_background_sensitive=false`); now EXIT=0 — augmented db count 3→6 (delta = 3 appended), overlaps unchanged at 2, contingency table internally consistent, p-values sensitive to the larger background.
- General fisher cases: query tail beyond db, `-m` merged mode, stdin query, and reversed a/b roles all report complete, consistent counts.
- Ordinary overlap commands preserved: shipped jaccard suite 15/15 ok, shipped intersect suite 85/85 ok, and hand-checked `intersect -wa -wb`, `-c`, and `window` against the fixture-shaped input produce identical, correct output (no phantom tail hits).
